footer.text: Built with Next.js and Supabase. MIT licensed and open for contributions.
footer.tagline: An open-source Next.js and Supabase starter kit built for learning. Practice on real features, send real pull requests, and grow as a developer.

home.subtitle: This starter kit gives developers a real, working codebase to practice on. Open pull requests, review code, pick up issues, and build features you have never tried before, all without touching a production app.

contribute.title: New here? Make your first contribution
contribute.subtitle: Never sent a pull request before? Follow these steps and you will have one merged today.
contribute.step1Desc: Open the Issues tab on GitHub and choose one labeled "good first issue" that you feel confident you can solve.
contribute.step2Desc: Click the Fork button at the top right of the repo. This creates your own copy of the project under your account.
contribute.step3Desc: Copy your fork's URL and run git clone on it to bring the code down to your machine.
contribute.step4Desc: Create a new branch, make the code changes described in the issue, and commit your work with a clear message.
contribute.step5Title: Push and open a pull request
contribute.step5Desc: Push your branch to your fork, then open a pull request back to the original repository.
contribute.step6Desc: Once your PR is reviewed and merged, it counts as a real contribution, shows on your GitHub activity graph, and adds hands-on practice and learning to your profile.
